purpose: Map real-world craft fabrication methods to asset-family build logic, drawing UI tags, Blender tool choices, and operator checks.

methods.plain_name: Full-scale tracing floor and template transfer

source_support.label: Drawing Matter medieval masons and tracing floors
source_support.support_summary: Supports full-scale geometric drawing surfaces as practical medieval masonry design and transfer tools.

source_support.label: Museum of the History of Science medieval drawing
source_support.support_summary: Supports compass/straightedge geometry as a construction basis for cathedral forms.

real_sequence: Establish centerlines, axes, and main proportional divisions.
Draw full-scale arcs, circles, offsets, and intersections.
Select the visible profiles from the construction geometry.
Make templates for repeated ribs, mouldings, arch stones, or tracery pieces.
Transfer template edges to stone or timber stock.
methods.mechanics: The construction drawing is not decoration. It is a source graph for repeatable parts, offsets, centers, radii, and cut profiles.
operator_checks: Are construction lines separated from visible lines?
Are repeated pieces driven by one template?
Are centers and radii recoverable from the drawing?
methods.repo_use: Foundation method for the future drafting UI and construction_graph_v0 schema.

methods.plain_name: Roughing, dressing, chiseling, and finishing stone

source_support.label: Regency Town House stone carving tools
source_support.support_summary: Supports point, claw, flat chisel, mallet, banker, and staged stone carving workflow.

source_support.label: Nasher Museum stone carving tools
source_support.support_summary: Supports tool-mark vocabulary and the physical sequence from rough shaping to refined carving.

real_sequence: Rough out the block and remove waste.
Dress the main faces and establish square/level reference faces.
Pitch or chamfer broad edges.
Use point and claw work to approach the profile.
Use flat chisels and abrasives for final arrises, grooves, and surface finish.
methods.mechanics: Stone detail reads through planes, arrises, tool marks, bevels, shadow grooves, and staged depth changes rather than arbitrary high-resolution sculpting.
operator_checks: Do bevels preserve shallow detail?
Do major faces stay readable?
Are grooves deep enough to catch shadow before texture work?
methods.repo_use: Default mental model for stone posts, plinths, capitals, trim, and wall blocks.

methods.plain_name: Tracery layout, template profiles, and cutout logic

source_support.label: Columbia Amiens dynamic geometry
source_support.support_summary: Supports Gothic composition through dynamic geometric layout and proportional relationships.

source_support.label: Drawing Matter medieval masons and tracing floors
source_support.support_summary: Supports layout-to-template workflow for masonry geometry.

real_sequence: Draw the opening, centerlines, circles, foils, cusps, and bars.
Select the lines that become stone bars or voids.
Make templates for repeated foils, lancets, and bar profiles.
Rough out openings and preserve the bar network.
Carve bevels, cusps, moulded arrises, and shadow lines.
methods.mechanics: Tracery is a selected-line problem: the construction grid is larger than the final visible stone, and omitted lines matter as much as selected ones.
operator_checks: Can every visible bar be traced to selected construction lines?
Do voids remain readable after beveling?
Are foils/cusps symmetrical where intended?
methods.repo_use: Core method for windows, blind panels, railing infill, and sacred-geometry-selected linework.

methods.plain_name: Arch centering, voussoir layout, and keystone sequence

source_support.label: Brick Industry Association Technical Notes on brick masonry arches
source_support.support_summary: Supports arch terminology, voussoir geometry, centering, and construction sequence concepts.

real_sequence: Set out springline, span, rise, intrados, and extrados.
Build temporary centering to hold arch stones/brick until self-supporting.
Lay voussoirs symmetrically from springing toward crown.
Set keystone/crown closure.
Remove centering only after the arch is stable.
methods.mechanics: Arch form depends on wedge action, compression, springline alignment, and temporary support. In game assets, this maps to visible voussoir segmentation, keystone emphasis, and springline sockets.
operator_checks: Does the arch have a readable springline?
Are voussoirs wedge-like or at least segmented?
Does the keystone/crown read from gameplay distance?
methods.repo_use: Default arch/door/window build plan before decorative tracery is added.

methods.plain_name: Rib vault layout, ribs, webbing, and bosses

source_support.label: Looking at Buildings rib vaults
source_support.support_summary: Supports rib vault anatomy: ribs, webbing, bosses, springing, and vault-bay vocabulary.

source_support.label: Drawing Matter medieval masons and tracing floors
source_support.support_summary: Supports full-scale geometric layout for ribs and vault components.

real_sequence: Lay out bay geometry, springing points, rib paths, and crown/boss centers.
Cut or prepare rib stones from templates.
Assemble ribs over centering or temporary support.
Fill webbing between ribs.
Add bosses or carved nodes at rib intersections.
methods.mechanics: The ribs are a path network; webbing is the surface between paths; bosses mark intersections and help make the structure legible.
operator_checks: Can the rib network be read before adding texture?
Do bosses sit at real intersections?
Are web cells separate from rib geometry?
methods.repo_use: Primary craft logic for future vaulted ceilings and sacred-geometry-to-dome experiments.

methods.plain_name: Frame-and-panel joinery with mortise and tenon logic

source_support.label: Common Woodworking mortise and tenon
source_support.support_summary: Supports mortise-and-tenon vocabulary and frame-joinery mechanics.

source_support.label: Woodworkers Institute frame and panel doors
source_support.support_summary: Supports frame-and-panel door construction concepts and member vocabulary.

real_sequence: Mark rails, stiles, shoulders, mortises, and tenons.
Cut mortises in stiles or posts.
Cut tenons on rails.
Fit shoulders flush and keep the frame square.
Insert floating or raised panel inside grooves.
methods.mechanics: A frame is a load/shape boundary; panels sit inside it. The joinery creates sockets, shoulders, reveals, and grooves that should appear in the model.
operator_checks: Are stiles and rails named separately?
Are grooves/reveals visible?
Can the panel read as separate from the frame?
methods.repo_use: Default method for doors, wood windows, wall panels, and furniture-like props.

methods.plain_name: Moulding profile layout and plane/router sequence

source_support.label: Encyclopaedia Britannica plane tool
source_support.support_summary: Supports hand plane vocabulary and the idea of shaped planes cutting profiles.

source_support.label: Woodworkers Institute moulding planes
source_support.support_summary: Supports moulding plane use for shaped profiles and traditional trim production.

real_sequence: Draw or choose the side profile.
Mark shoulders, fillets, rabbets, coves, rounds, beads, and flats.
Remove waste with straight/rabbet cuts.
Shape coves/rounds/beads with profile tools.
Scrape/sand and fit as trim.
methods.mechanics: Moulding is a side-profile stack. A complex trim often comes from simple flats, rounds, coves, beads, and shadow grooves in sequence.
operator_checks: Does the side profile read before texture?
Are beads/coves named as profile zones?
Are shadow grooves deep enough to survive bevels?
methods.repo_use: Core method for ornament railings, cap lips, bases, trim, and plinth stacks.

methods.plain_name: Heated bar, bending jig, scrollwork, and repeated iron ornament

source_support.label: The Wroughtworks past and present methods
source_support.support_summary: Supports traditional wrought iron processes, hand forging, and architectural ironwork context.

source_support.label: National Park Service preservation brief on historic ornamental metal
source_support.support_summary: Supports ornamental metal preservation vocabulary and architectural metal component awareness.

real_sequence: Heat bar stock until workable.
Taper, flatten, or upset ends if needed.
Bend around scroll jigs or anvil horns.
Repeat mirrored scrolls or modules.
Join with collars, rivets, forge welds, or mechanical fasteners.
methods.mechanics: Iron ornament is path and repetition driven: bar thickness, bend radius, mirrored scrolls, collars, and connection nodes carry the look.
operator_checks: Do scrolls look like bent bar rather than flat drawing lines?
Are collars/joints named?
Can repeated modules be changed from one source curve?
methods.repo_use: Default method for iron railings, gates, grilles, scroll brackets, and lantern cages.

methods.plain_name: Rivets, collars, tenons, and mechanical iron joints

source_support.label: National Park Service preservation brief on historic ornamental metal
source_support.support_summary: Supports historic architectural metal components and preservation-sensitive metal joinery vocabulary.

source_support.label: The Wroughtworks resources
source_support.support_summary: Supports traditional forged ironwork and hand-worked joining context.

real_sequence: Lay out crossing bars and join points.
Punch or drill holes where rivets are needed.
Add collars around bundled or crossing members.
Set rivets or peen tenons.
Dress and finish edges.
methods.mechanics: Joints are visible logic. Collars and rivets should be modeled as named connector details, not random beads.
operator_checks: Do rivets/collars align with actual intersections?
Are join points part of the drawing graph?
Can LOD remove small rivets without losing main bars?
methods.repo_use: Adds believable mechanics to metal railings, gates, hardware, and mechanisms.

methods.plain_name: Sheet-metal raising, bossing, and low relief

source_support.label: Victoria and Albert Museum metalworking techniques
source_support.support_summary: Supports repoussé, chasing, engraving, and metal surface-relief technique vocabulary.

real_sequence: Draw or transfer the relief pattern.
Support the metal sheet on pitch or a forming surface.
Raise broad forms from the back or sink from the front.
Chase crisp lines and details.
Planish or finish exposed surfaces.
methods.mechanics: Relief is layered depth: broad pushed forms, crisp chased lines, edge highlights, and material-specific deformation.
operator_checks: Are broad relief forms separated from fine chased lines?
Do highlights work before procedural texture?
Can low hardware drop fine marks but keep bosses?
methods.repo_use: Useful for metal door panels, armor, treasure props, sconces, and decorative trim.
